target_customer: Individuals and parents who want to cut compulsive phone use; consumers pay via in-app subscription, later a family-focused offering
problem: People lose hours to compulsive phone use and built-in screen time tools are easy to bypass. Clearspace adds friction and blocking so users can control how time is spent online.
business_model: Consumer mobile subscription with free tier and in-app purchases
product_category: Consumer screen time and digital wellbeing app

founders.name: Royce Branning
founders.background_notes: A search summary of a Notre Dame Idea Center profile says he began the app as a side project while at Quicken and resigned in May 2021. The profile page itself returned 404 when opened, so the employer is lightly sourced. Education not confirmed.

founders.name: Oliver Hill
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as cofounder and CTO. No background found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: Blocking apps on iOS depends on Apple Screen Time APIs and requires careful engineering around platform limits; the core is a mobile app plus backend, with harder parts in reliable enforcement across devices.

defensibility.rationale: Features such as app blocking and timers are copyable and the platform owners ship similar tools; differentiation rests on execution, content and brand with parents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple and Google both ship free screen time controls, and many third party apps already existed. No evidence found of either copying Clearspace specifically.

market_need_then: Widespread public concern about phone addiction after the pandemic. The founder says the app grew from his own struggle, and the first users came from the App Store organically.

branding.domain_note: Company site is clearspace.org; the app marketing has also used getclearspace.com per aggregator listings. History not sourced.

identity.logo: Light lockup wordmark; design not described by sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and reassuring, written from one parent to another

branding.brand_signature: Tagline Less screen time, more life (later more childhood)
branding.community_and_virality: Site lists press from Wirecutter, Forbes, Business Insider, The Atlantic and New York Magazine; a search summary says it was featured on the Huberman Lab podcast and in the New York Times. A 2026 source mentions a separate app called Ozone Family.

brand_strength.rationale: Credible press mentions and a clean message, but the name is generic and shared with other products such as the Clearspace ClearSpace enterprise product, so the brand was only moderately distinctive.

outcome_analysis: Clearspace is still active and has not reported an exit or shutdown. It entered YC in Winter 2023 with an App Store consumer app, and sources suggest steady press, and a later move toward family products and an agent based intentionality layer in 2026. Funding is not verified beyond a single aggregator figure, so its trajectory cannot yet be judged against outcomes.
